bullets: **Localism:** hiring your own PhDs and colleagues
**Social origin:** who reaches the doctorate and the faculty
**Ethnic and racial discrimination:** what France can and cannot measure
**Nationality and language**
**Prestige:** famous names, elite institutions, Paris
**Geography:** high- vs low-income countries

Sources, data and figures: github.com/jmourabarbosa/gender-bias

slides.title: 1. Localism and inbreeding
slides.sub: Hiring your own PhDs and your own colleagues

slides.title: About 1 in 5 new MCF are hired where they did their PhD; over half of new PR where they were already MCF
bullets: 2024 recruits: **23%** of new MCF local, **54%** of new PR local
MCF local share has stayed between 17% and 23% since 2018
The PR jump in 2022 partly reflects a change of definition
About 10% of posts are filled by transfer (mutation)

slides.title: Local candidates have about 10 times the odds of being hired as MCF
bullets: MCF hiring 2017-2024: odds ratio **9.5 to 10.7** for local candidates
Physiology about 29; mathematics below 1
2008 study: 6.3% of local applications succeeded vs 0.24% of external ones
refs: Godechot, Issiakou, Renisio & Rougier (2025) Books & Ideas
Godechot & Louvet (2008) La Vie des idées

slides.title: Spain is more inbred: 73% of university staff teach where they got their PhD
bullets: Spain: **72.9%** (2020-21), unchanged since 2015
Spain 2006: 96% of permanent-post winners already worked there
Portugal: about 68% (secondary source)
Mexico: inbred faculty publish 15% fewer peer-reviewed articles
refs: Spanish ministry, Estadística de Personal de las Universidades

slides.title: 2. Social origin
slides.sub: Who reaches the doctorate and the faculty

slides.title: Workers' children are 12% of licence students but 6% of doctoral students
bullets: Children of senior managers: 29% in licence, **40%** in doctorate (2019-20)
Doctoral students: 41% have a manager parent, 8% a manual-worker parent
No published data on the social origin of French academics
refs: Observatoire des inégalités, from MESR data

slides.title: Grandes écoles: 64% of students come from very privileged homes, vs 23% of their age group
bullets: ENS: **72%** very privileged
ENS 2024: children of senior managers 65%, of manual workers 2%
Composition barely changed between 2009 and 2024
refs: Bonneau, Charousset, Grenet & Thebault (2021) IPP report 30

slides.title: 22% of US faculty have a parent with a PhD; at top institutions, about a third
bullets: Share rises with institutional prestige
US economics PhDs: **48%** have a parent with a graduate degree
UK: 42% of Royal Society and British Academy fellows were privately educated, vs 7% of the population
refs: Morgan et al. (2022) Nature Human Behaviour

slides.title: 3. Ethnic and racial discrimination
slides.sub: What France can and cannot measure

slides.title: France bans ethnic statistics, but surveys show children of African immigrants report 2-3 times more discrimination
bullets: Public statistics cannot use racial categories; surveys may ask about origin
TeO2 (2019-20): **42%** (children of immigrants from sub-Saharan Africa) vs 15% (no migration background)
No data on the ethnic composition of French academic staff

slides.title: Master's programmes replied less often to applicants with North-African names
bullets: Testing on 600+ master's programmes (2021): **69.7%** vs **61.1%** positive replies
Largest gaps in law, economics, management and science
Labour market testing: callbacks 33.3% vs 22.8%

slides.title: In one French university, 28% of staff of immigrant descent reported racist treatment vs 5% of the majority
bullets: ACADISCRI staff survey 2019-20 (small sample, 278 staff)
Few victims report it: **13%** of students vs 47% of staff
13.8% of LGBTQ+ staff report LGBT-phobic treatment (same survey)
refs: Cognet, Hajjat, Hamel et al. (2022) ACADISCRI

slides.title: At NIH, Black applicants' grant success has stayed 1.7 times lower than White applicants'
bullets: Topic choice explains about 20% of the gap
Black applicants' success rate about 75% of White applicants' after controls

slides.title: 4. Nationality and language
slides.sub: Foreign researchers and non-native English speakers

slides.title: Foreign nationals are 42% of new PhDs in France but 8% of tenured faculty
bullets: 21% of permanent research recruits (2022)
CNRS: about a third of recruits are foreign (CEO); MESR counts 24.5% for EPST recruits
CNRS interviews are held in French by default

slides.title: Foreigners are 23.5% of new MCF but 7.9% of new PR
bullets: Gap stable 2020-2024
Among PR hired from outside the MCF corps, 31-40% are foreign
Talent-passport visas can take about 5 months (one testimony)

slides.title: Non-native English speakers face more language rejections and more work
bullets: Up to **90.8%** more time to read a paper in English
Researchers who had a paper rejected for its English: 38% (moderate proficiency) vs 14% (native)
Authors from France chose double-blind review 8% of the time, from India 32%

slides.title: Reviewers often share a country with US and Chinese authors, rarely with low-income-country authors
bullets: A same-country reviewer raises acceptance by **4.78 points**
eLife: 39.2% of US submissions sent to review vs 12.6% from China

slides.title: 5. Prestige
slides.sub: Famous names, elite institutions, and Paris

slides.title: Same paper: 65% of reviewers rejected it under a junior author's name, 22% under a Nobel laureate's
bullets: 534 reviews of one manuscript, author shown or hidden
Anonymized: 48% reject
Single-blind conference reviewers favoured famous authors (OR **1.63**)

slides.title: 80% of US faculty trained at 20% of universities
bullets: Top 25% of institutions produce 71-86% of faculty, depending on field
Early-career grant winners just above the threshold got more than twice the later funding of near-misses
refs: Bol, de Vaan & van de Rijt (2018) PNAS

slides.title: Île-de-France concentrates French research money and prizes
bullets: **42%** of business R&D spending (2024)
About a third of French publications (2019)
4 of the first 8 Idex were in Île-de-France
ERC Starting Grants 2024: 25 of 49 French winners hosted by the CNRS

slides.title: 6. Geography
slides.sub: Research from high- vs low-income countries

slides.title: Clinicians rated the same abstract higher when told it came from a rich country
bullets: 347 English clinicians, same abstracts, randomised source country
Relevance +4.5 points (out of 100) for a high-income source
Implicit association test: 86% of researchers lean 'rich country = good research'
Systematic review: 2 of 3 randomised trials found bias
refs: Harris et al. (2017) Globalization and Health
Skopec et al. (2020) Research Integrity and Peer Review

slides.title: Research done in Africa: half of the papers have an African first author
bullets: 1,182 papers on 6 infectious diseases, 1980-2016
African last author: 41.3%
Coral-reef papers in Indonesia and the Philippines: about 40% had no local author
Papers from peripheral countries are under-cited, and the gap is growing
refs: Mbaye et al. (2019) BMJ Global Health
Gomez, Herman & Parigi (2022) Nature Human Behaviour

slides.title: Open-access fees push out low-income authors
bullets: Elsevier mirror journals: 0.5% of APC articles had low-income first authors, vs 2.4% in subscription versions
One APC can cost about 3 months of a Ukrainian professor's salary
Visas: 4 of 10 invited speakers from low-income countries got EU visas
refs: Smith et al. (2022) Quantitative Science Studies

slides.title: 7. Precarity, age and career stage
slides.sub: Fewer posts, later hiring, more contracts

slides.title: French universities published 21% fewer MCF posts in 2024 than in 2008
bullets: Candidates per MCF post: 4.7 (2008), peak 7.7 (2021), 5.0 (2024)

slides.title: A quarter of French university teachers are on fixed-term contracts
bullets: 2024: **21,080** contract teachers vs 61,879 tenured
Excludes about 164,500 hourly lecturers (vacataires)
One deputy's worked example: €8.37 per hour actually worked for a vacataire
81% of first-year doctoral students are funded; 53% in humanities

slides.title: New MCF are hired at 35, and 42% come straight from a postdoc
bullets: Sciences and technology: **67%** were postdocs just before hiring
CNRS: researchers recruited at 34.4 on average (2020)
CNRS contract staff on own funds: 23% (2013) → 29% (2023)
US cancer research: age at first R01 grant 36.2 (1990) → 44.9 (2016)

slides.title: Half of a 2010s cohort of scientists left within 5 years, vs 35 years in the 1960s
bullets: Astronomy, ecology and robotics publication careers
US postdocs: **17%** eventually land a tenure-track job
51% of postdocs have considered leaving science over mental health (2020 survey)
refs: Andalib, Ghaffarzadegan & Larson (2018) Syst Res Behav Sci

slides.title: 8. Disability and LGBTQ+
French research institutions employ fewer disabled staff than the 6% legal quota
bullets: Higher education and research: **4.49%** (union figure; no official national rate online)
NIH applicants reporting a disability: 1.9% (2008) → 1.2% (2018)
US: disabled people are 11% of science and engineering PhDs but 3% of the workforce (two surveys)

slides.title: A third of trans and non-binary students have faced sexual violence in French higher education
bullets: **33%** vs 24% of women and 9% of men
13.8% of LGBTQ+ university staff report LGBT-phobic treatment
US STEM: 22% of LGBTQ professionals thought about leaving vs 15%
UK physical sciences: 28% of LGBT+ scientists considered leaving
